items.title: The 'hands-off' doctrine in election disputes: A case for reconsideration
items.summary: Democracy, as the Supreme Court has repeatedly reminded us, is not merely an incident of our constitutional scheme, but a part of its basic structure. In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu , the Supreme Court held that ‘democracy’ and ‘free and fair elections’ are inseparable twins. In Rajbala v. State of Haryana , the Supreme Court described the right to vote and right to contest in elections to local bodies as constitutional rights. Earlier, in Jyoti Basu v. Debi Ghosal , the Supreme Court held that the said right is neither a fundamental right nor a common law right, but a statutory right. Rajbala reads it to constitutional rank at least in elections to panchayats. Nothing in this article turns on winning that classificatory battle. Constitutional right or statutory right, the interest at stake is the same and the Court’s own basic structure jurisprudence has already told us how much it weighs. Yet, when disputes touching upon the electoral process are actually brought before the constitutional courts, a curious reluctance sets in. items.title: Telangana SIR: Over 73 lakh voters marked absent, dead, shifted, or duplicate
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The enumeration forms of 2.64 crore voters in Telangana have been digitised as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, according to State Chief Electoral Officer C Sudarshan Reddy. The CEO’s office said on Tuesday, August 11, that 78.30% of the state’s 3.38 crore voters had their enumeration forms digitised. The update came a day after the door-to-door verification exercise by booth-level officers concluded on Monday. Around 73.39 lakh enumeration forms, or 21.70% of the total, remain undigitised and have been classified as “uncollectable”. Of these, 9.22 lakh voters have been marked as dead, while 11.25 lakh were classified as absent or untraceable. Another 45.18 lakh voters were found to have permanently shifted, while 6.70 lakh were marked as already enrolled. The CEO’s office also placed 1.02 lakh voters under the “others” category, without specifying what this classification means. Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri recorded the highest rate of digitisation in the state at 94.31%, while Hyderabad recorded the lowest at 58.89%. Rank holders on the Kerala Public Service Commission’s (PSC) list for appointment to lower primary schools ended a 13-day indefinite hunger strike on Tuesday, August 11, following talks with the government. The hunger strike was part of a 37-day-long protest organised by the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teacher (LPST) PSC Rank Holders' Association. S Valarmathi, the association secretary, broke her fast by accepting a drink of water from General Education Minister N Samsudheen. The government has sought 45 days to examine the protesters' demands. “I am happy that we were able to conclude the discussions on a positive note. The hunger strike has now been called off,” said Valarmathi after the meeting with the Minister. The rank holders’ indefinite protest outside the Kerala Secretariat in Thiruvananthapuram, demanded immediate appointment orders from the May 2025 Kerala PSC rank list. They also demanded extending the validity of the rank list, as many of the rank holders on the current list have not got jobs. items.title: Wildlife department to probe origin of lar gibbon seen in actor Vikram’s video
items.summary: Actor Chiyaan Vikram has drawn the attention of wildlife authorities and conservationists after sharing a video of himself interacting with a lar gibbon. The species is a threatened primate protected under international wildlife trade regulations. The video, which Vikram posted on social media, showed him playing with a well-grown lar gibbon. It quickly went viral, but also triggered questions over how the exotic animal came to be in a private setting in Chennai and whether its owner possesses the documents required to legally keep it. The lar gibbon, scientifically known as Hylobates lar, is native to Southeast Asia and is listed under Appendix I of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). The species is also classified as a Schedule IV animal under India's amended Wildlife Protection Act. Under CITES, Appendix I covers species facing the highest level of protection and places stringent restrictions on international commercial trade. Possession of an exotic animal in India can also be subject to domestic requirements concerning its acquisition, registration, transfer and supporting documentation. items.title: Inside Jharkhand’s assembly gherao: Lathicharge, tear gas and conflicting claims
items.summary: Thousands of students from all districts of Jharkhand marched on the state assembly in Ranchi on Monday, demanding the cancellation of exams conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission over alleged paper leaks and irregularities. They also demanded a CBI probe into the allegations. Despite prohibitory orders under BNSS section 163 and heavy barricading with barbed wire, protesters broke through the security cordons and reached the assembly complex. The police responded with water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge, leaving several students injured. The police claimed that protesters pelted stones, injuring several security personnel.
